_README: Passed via --models-config to detect.py or detect_multiturn.py; without that
flag both scripts use the 10 built-ins hard-coded in detect.py, so the
model_id (exact API id), key_env, endpoint, stream, extra_body,
'dashscope3' — Bailian issues WORKSPACE endpoints, so each DashScope entry
must name the slot matching its key_env), a full base URL, or a ${ENV_VAR}
reference resolved at load time (keeps hosts out of the repo).
The first 11 entries mirror detect.py exactly. The NEW-DETECTOR-* entries are
placeholders: rename them, fill in model_id/endpoint, set disabled=false.

detectors.name: gpt-6
detectors.notes: New OpenAI detector (GPT-6 family). Confirm with: check_models.py --list --provider openai --grep gpt-6. If the id needs a reasoning setting, put it in extra_body, e.g. {"reasoning_effort": "medium"}.

detectors.name: grok-new
detectors.notes: New xAI detector. Confirm with: check_models.py --list --provider xai. Rename the entry to the real id so result filenames stay self-describing.

detectors.name: qwen3.8
detectors.notes: New Qwen detector (3.8 family). Confirm with: check_models.py --list --provider dashscope --grep qwen3.8. DashScope thinking models usually REQUIRE stream=true; if the probe returns a 400 about streaming, that is the field to flip.

detectors.name: gemini-new
detectors.notes: New Gemini detector. Confirm with: check_models.py --list --provider gemini --grep gemini. Set gemini_thinking_level only to override the vendor default.
